title: The Stone's house at Caol leathan rebuilt
summary: The order of the Stone rebuilds its house at Caol leathan at its own cost, raising a bell tower over the western gable; the town sets its market and its two courts by the bell from that year on.

title: Oighrig nic Mhathain named toll-mistress
summary: Oighrig nic Mhathain, nine years the market clerk of Dùn chrom and one-and-thirty that year, is asked by the council's eastern factor to keep the new fair to be held at the ford by Muileann òg, and takes the post, leaving her own scales to a niece she has trained two summers at her elbow.

title: The fair-field marked out at Muileann òg
summary: Oighrig nic Mhathain walks the ground at Muileann òg with a length of cord and a stick through the summer, marking the stalls, the beast-pens and the corner where a court might sit, before any building has been raised there.

title: The court of the fair roofed
summary: Carpenters of Dùn chrom finish a plain roofed frame, open on three sides, at the field's corner nearest the ford, a fortnight before the fair is to open; it is the only building the state gives the fair in its first year.

title: Oighrig writes the fair's three rules
summary: Over three evenings by rush-light Oighrig nic Mhathain writes the fair's rules in her own plain hand: a stall-fee in coin, a court of the fair to sit each day of the gathering, and Tuathaich goods to be sold only through licensed Dia-thìreach factors, on the council's own instruction.

title: The first factors licensed for northern goods
summary: The council licenses four merchant houses of the eastern shires to stand factors' stalls at Muileann òg and sell Tuathaich goods under their own names for a share of the price; Oighrig nic Mhathain enters their names under a heading of her own, Bàillidhean na Fèille.

title: The court of the fair's first sitting
summary: On the fair's opening morning, 16 an Dàmhair, Oighrig nic Mhathain's court hears its first case, a dispute over a barrel of salt fish, and settles it within the hour by weighing the barrel herself; she writes it into her book as setting the pattern for every case after it.

title: The spoil-stone case judged by a smith's eye
summary: A Cathair mhòr coal-carter brings a Sloc Mòr merchant's load of spoil-stone dressed to pass for coal-iron before the court of the fair; Oighrig nic Mhathain, having no forge of her own, sends the load to Muileann òg's one smith and fines the merchant by his judgment.

title: David Hale's wool turned away at the gate
summary: David Hale of Caol mhòr brings four sacks of his father's wool to the fair's ninth day, the first cart from the Moot's own provinces to try it; Oighrig nic Mhathain reads him her own third clause and turns him to a factor's stall, where his wool sells for some fifth part less than a northern market would have given.

title: The fair's road metalled past Dùn chrom
summary: In am Faoilleach the last stretch of the road from Cathair dhearg to Muileann òg is metalled for the fair's carts; the carters already call it Rathad na Fèille before the state gives it a name of its own.

title: Dùn chrom's gate-toll raises the fair's wall
summary: The toll taken at Dùn chrom's gate on the fair's road pays, that same winter, for a new wall along the town's southern side, finished by an Cèitean; the townsfolk call it the fair's wall, and the carters call the gate by another name.

title: The Moot's letter against the factor rule filed
summary: Walter Hale writes to the council on the Moot's behalf naming the factor rule a licence laid across a trade the north carried on unaided, and asks it looked at again; the council answers, months on, that the rule stands and will not be reconsidered inside the year, and the letter is filed with the Moot's earlier ones.

title: The fair's rules confirmed and read aloud
summary: In an Lùnastal a council clerk reads Oighrig nic Mhathain's rules aloud before the gathered factors and maoir of the eastern shires, word for word as she wrote them, and asks whether the reading matches her own book; she tells him it does.

title: The first fair runs a fortnight
summary: The first fair at Muileann òg runs a fortnight, with wool from the western shires, the Sloc Mòr's coal from the east, Baile chiar's cloth and salt from the coastal pans on the one field, more trade than Oighrig nic Mhathain had seen gathered in nine years of market days.

title: Pipers from Baile chiar at the first fair
summary: Pipers from Baile chiar play for coin at the far corner of the first fair's field, over the woodsmoke and wet wool and the coal carts' black dust, through the low constant argument of buying and selling in half a dozen tongues.
